messages:
jamie: Customer ACME reporting parse failures when using structured JSON mode with streaming. Their parser throws: 'Unexpected token' after ~1KB. Happens only when they stream long inputs and include Windows CRLFs. Request ID: rq_0a1b2c3d
liz: Can you attach the raw streaming chunks the customer captured (exact bytes)? Also what SDK/version and whether there's a proxy/ingress.
jamie: They captured it; pasting two consecutive chunks they saved:
marco: Reproduced locally — payload is being split across chunk boundary in the middle of an escape sequence. Raw captured chunks below (verbatim):
```
chunk 1: {"items":[{"type":"message","text":"First line\r\nSecond li
```
```
chunk 2: ne\", "id":1}] }
```
vasu: Because the backslash-escaped CRLF ("\\r\\n") got split, the incremental JSON stream parser on the client sees an invalid token (literal CR or unescaped n). The runtime currently just streams raw bytes; we don't guarantee chunk boundaries aligned to JSON tokens.
alex: Short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to use non-streaming mode or normalize CRLF -> LF before sending. 2) Client should buffer until a full JSON object is received. Long-term: add runtime safety to avoid splitting inside backslash escapes or multibyte UTF-8 sequences; add unit test for chunk-boundary escape splits.
jamie: Repro curl we'll ask them to run:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d @prompt.txt https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?structured=json
```
where prompt.txt contains CRLF line endings.
liz: Filed INF-1422 and assigned to eng-runtime. Support notified customer of workaround (disable streaming/normalize CRLF). Customer confirmed workaround fixed parse error. ETA for runtime patch: ~48h.
support-bot: ticket INF-1422 created by liz
jamie: closing loop with customer tomorrow; marking resolved for now :thumbsup:
